what: Planner deferred tap_multicast_per_group by ranking redundant tap traffic in BYTES (<=1.1% of DRAM bytes). On device, 110 cores x 128 x 32 B tap reads (~14k tiny DRAM requests) stalled each reader 3-80 us before its first input row; DRAM behaved request-rate-bound, not byte-bound. Fixing it was the largest single 004 win (185.9 -> 152.9 us).
suggest: In blocking-model / data-movement budget guidance: count DRAM REQUESTS (not just bytes) for reuse-shared operands fetched as many sub-64B reads per core; treat cores_per_group x tiny-request fan-in as critical-path unless measured otherwise.
